title: Six Months In, Unemployment Hits 9.5% — Highest in Five Years
detail: Marking six months since Kast's March 11 inauguration, national unemployment reached 9.5% in the May–July quarter (about 981,000 people), the highest rate in five years and the highest in Latin America, hitting women and young people hardest; informal employment stood at 26.5%. The Central Bank's September Informe de Política Monetaria (IPoM) cut its 2026 growth forecast from 1%–1.75% to 0.25%–0.75%, citing weakening demand, a deteriorating labor market, falling business confidence and the drag from fuel-price increases, while projecting a rebound to 2%–3% growth in 2027 and 2.25%–3.25% in 2028 aided by reconstruction-law spending. Kast, who had campaigned on cutting unemployment to 6% and creating the most jobs in a decade, acknowledged his government had not yet solved the problem and ordered ministers to draft a short-term emergency jobs plan.

sources.name: Diario y Radio Universidad de Chile

title: Government Departures Reach 48 as Coquimbo Energy Seremi Resigns
detail: Fabián Páez, Coquimbo's regional energy secretary (seremi) since March 30, resigned September 17 after the Comptroller's Office (Contraloría) objected that he did not meet the position's academic requirements; the Mining seremi, Juan Carlos Salinas, assumed the energy portfolio on an interim basis. Páez's exit was the 38th seremi-level departure and the 48th total departure (including ministers, undersecretaries and other officials) from the Kast administration since it took office in March, following two other regional secretary resignations earlier the same week — Antofagasta's housing seremi (Sep 14, over social-housing management failures) and Araucanía's health seremi (Sep 15, over a remark comparing elderly-care facility closures to waste disposal).
